summary: self-sign ships hidden eval() sink on undocumented third argument of generate()
details: self-sign is a typosquat of the legitimate `selfsigned` package (impersonating maintainer José F. Romaniello). index.js exports.generate accepts an undocumented third `defaults` parameter that strips `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` PEM headers, base64-decodes the remainder, and passes the decoded string to eval(). The upstream source shipped alongside as original.txt does not contain this branch, confirming the code was added on top of the legitimate package. The README has been rewritten so every documented call ends with `,null)`, normalizing a third argument at call sites so downstream applications route data through the eval sink. Any consumer that forwards attacker-influenced certificate-shaped data as the third argument to selfsign.generate() executes arbitrary JavaScript in the host process.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
